references.text: The Mount of Olives is mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy as the place where the Lord will stand on the last day. Jesus is approaching precisely the descent from the Mount of Olives ([ref:Zech 14:4|Zechariah 14:4]).
The immediate context describing Jesus' route toward Jerusalem via the Mount of Olives ([ref:Luke 19:29-30|Luke 19:29-30]).
The continuation of this praise, where the disciples cry out, "Blessed is he who comes, the king, in the name of the Lord!" ([ref:Luke 19:38|Luke 19:38]).
Matthew's parallel account of the crowd praising God as Jesus entered Jerusalem ([ref:Matt 21:8-9|Matthew 21:8-9]).
Mark's parallel account of the entry into Jerusalem with praise and homage ([ref:Mark 11:8-10|Mark 11:8-10]).
John's account of the crowd meeting Jesus with praise as he entered Jerusalem ([ref:John 12:12-13|John 12:12-13]).
Jesus had performed mighty deeds (δυνάμεις) that the disciples had witnessed, including in the cities mentioned here ([ref:Luke 10:13|Luke 10:13]).
The angels' praise at Jesus' birth forms a parallel – a heavenly host praises God with a loud voice, just as the disciples now do at the entry ([ref:Luke 2:13-14|Luke 2:13-14]).
The Pharisees ask Jesus to rebuke the disciples for this praise, but Jesus answers that the stones would cry out if the disciples were silent ([ref:Luke 19:39-40|Luke 19:39-40]).
"Who can declare the Lord's mighty deeds?" – the disciples praised God for all the mighty works they had seen ([ref:Ps 106:2|Psalms 106:2]).
The messianic psalm that forms the basis of the disciples' praise: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord" ([ref:Ps 118:26|Psalms 118:26]).
